news.title: Spain Stands With Ceuta as Football Federation Brings World Cup Trophy to City
news.lede: “Spain is Ceuta, and Ceuta is Spain.” That was the message from Spanish Football Federation president Rafael Louzán during a visit to the autonomous city, where the RFEF delegation came to show its support for the local community during a difficult period. Louzán was joined by Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente, general secretary Álvaro de Miguel and sporting director Aitor Karanka. The delegation was welcomed by Ceuta president Juan Jesús Vivas, who received the World Cup trophy won by Spain this summer.

news.title: Brazil great Formiga says 2027 World Cup will ‘change players’ lives’
news.lede: SAO PAULO: Brazil legend Formiga believes next year’s Women’s World Cup in the country will be “an opportunity to change the lives of countless” players in South America. Former midfielder Formiga scored 29 goals in over 200 appearances for the Selecao before retiring aged 43 in 2021. The 2027 tournament will mark the first time the World Cup has been held in Latin America, in a country where women were banned from playing football as recently as 1979. “We have a tremendous opportunity to change the landscape of South American football,” Formiga told AFP at the “Esporte Cria” event organised by the Brazilian Olympic Committee in Sao Paulo.

news.title: ‘Advertise the sport, study the great footballing schools’ - Brazil's World Cup-winner Cafu's advice to Indian football
news.lede: Former Brazil captain Cafu on Friday said the Indian football will have to advertise the sport and study the great footballing schools to grow as a footballing nation. Despite being a country of 1.4 billion, India are yet to qualify for the World Cup, even after the FIFA expanded the tournament to 48 teams, thus opening new opportunities for smaller nations.The 56-year-old Cafu pointed at how smaller nations like Curacao and Cape Verde “played on equal terms” with bigger teams in the FIFA World Cup 2026 In the USA, Mexico and Canada. While Curacao exited in the group stage, Cape Verde made it the round of 32 before going down fighting 2-3 against Lionel Messi's Argentina at Miami Gardens." Today, everyone plays on equal terms.

news.title: UEFA and STRAUSS partner to elevate refereeing across European football
news.lede: The German company will support European football’s governing body in referee development, increasing visibility for match officials and bringing fans closer to the people behind the whistle. UEFA and STRAUSS, a leading brand for workwear, safety equipment and work-wearables, today announced a new partnership dedicated to supporting and developing refereeing across European football, reinforcing the vital role match officials play at every level of the game. Under the agreement, STRAUSS will become the first-ever official partner of UEFA refereeing, with its brand integrated across a range of refereeing activities and competitions.

news.title: The best do not always win the World Cup: Cafu | Football News
news.lede: Mumbai: On a stage at a college atrium, Cafu soaked in the adulation. Students, brandishing any Brazilian jersey they could find – from the present selection with ‘Neymar Jr’ printed on the back to quite a few with ‘Ronaldo’ – cheered him on. Cafu beckoned a few to toss their shirts forward for him to sign and send back.And then his eye caught a replica World Cup trophy. More silver than gold, it was handed over to him to pose with.

news.title: Basketball: D’Tigress Beaten by South Korea in World Cup Opener
news.lede: South Korea handily defeated Nigeria 99–81 on the opening day of the 2026 Women’s Basketball World Cup in Berlin. This Group B opener lived up to all expectations, delivering a high-scoring offensive spectacle at the Uber Arena. The African champions, however, gave their opponents a run for their money in the first half thanks to Amy Okonkwo’s physical presence. Trailing by one point at halftime, the South Koreans bounced back after the break with formidable outside shooting.
